title: Analysis & Findings
description: Source-linked analysis, including discrimination, one-vs-both, and conservative checklist.

rows.label: Normal local increase
rows.value: 1.6% or less on each eligible unit
rows.notes: Once every 12 months; license; notice.

rows.label: State cap is not a substitute
rows.value: AB 1482 8.8% does not apply to SF Rent Ordinance rent-controlled units
rows.notes: Local protections remain.

rows.label: No federal rent cap found
rows.notes: HUD FMR/SAFMR are voucher standards.

rows.label: Disparate-impact risk
rows.value: Liability can exist without intent; neutral criteria and no less discriminatory alternative matter
rows.notes: Current eCFR as of 11/04/2026.

rows.label: FEHA broader classes
rows.value: Source of income, retaliation, perception/association and aggregate-income rules apply
rows.notes: State overlay.

rows.label: Local harassment overlay
rows.value: Bad-faith coercion/discrimination prohibited
rows.notes: Larson footnote flagged.

rows.label: Unit 1 roommate change
rows.value: Not a basis for extra rent; vacancy-decontrol eligibility unverified
rows.notes: No market-rate reset recommended.

rows.label: One vs both
rows.value: Raising both is not officially required; identical neutral policy reduces disparate-treatment optics
rows.notes: Document neutral eligibility/anniversary reasons; no guarantee.

rows.label: Unit 2 long tenure
rows.value: Mere below-market rent is not extraordinary circumstances
rows.notes: Special Circumstances petition required for comparable-rent reset.

rows.label: Banked increases
rows.value: Cannot be inferred because rent history is unverified
rows.notes: Blank and flagged.

rows.label: Corporate figures
rows.value: Portfolio-level disclosures are evidence of practice, not legal benchmarks
rows.notes: Not SF-specific.

rows.label: Individual figures
rows.value: June 2024 workload is narrow formal-petition evidence
rows.notes: No generalization.

rows.label: Tenant-lawyer review
rows.value: Checklist capable of review; no approval claimed
rows.notes: TRC is eviction-focused.

rows.label: Conservative compliance checklist
rows.value: At most ordinary 1.6% annual allowable increase (or less) on each eligible unit, identical written neutral policy, license, notice, dates, calculations, recordkeeping
rows.notes: No guarantee of no complaint/lawsuit.

rows.label: Flagged items do not block
rows.value: All flagged items published with official source links
rows.notes: Needs review does not block the merge; the live count is shown on the dashboard (flag F37).

rows.label: What a tenant-side reviewer would test
rows.value: 1) current license on the effective date, 2) correct rate for that date, 3) 12 months since the last increase, 4) base rent only and no rounding up, 5) notice contents, lead time and delivery, 6) no extra charge for an added roommate, 7) no retaliation or bad-faith harassment
rows.notes: Each item is checkable against the official pages linked here; passing them is not a certification of lawfulness.

rows.label: The license is a precondition, not paperwork
rows.value: An increase noticed while the unit is unlicensed may be null and void or unenforceable with refund exposure, and the Rent Board issues noncompliance notices; its January 2026 minutes record more than 23,000 licenses
rows.notes: Checks should look at the effective date, not today's status.

rows.label: Individual owners are not exempt
rows.value: The requirement follows rent-controlled status; there is no owner-size exemption, and buildings under 10 units have reported since March 1, 2023
rows.notes: Direct answer to the owner's question.

rows.label: A banked total can exceed 10%
rows.value: Adding a correctly banked percentage to the current annual increase can push one notice above 10%, which then needs 90-day notice
rows.notes: No banked amount is asserted for either unit; pending File 261020 could affect banked increases (F46).

rows.label: The filing itself is public
rows.value: Housing Inventory information is public, so reporting publishes the owner's name and business contact information
rows.notes: Privacy consideration; the filing is still required for a license.

rows.label: Two distinct registrations with the Rent Board
rows.value: Housing Inventory reporting produces the license at no charge; the Rent Board Fee is a separate $59.00-per-unit annual payment. Paying the fee does not replace reporting.
rows.notes: Both are due around March 1 but are not interchangeable (F33).

rows.label: License timing and retaliation risk
rows.value: A license that exists today does not validate a notice whose effective date preceded it. California Civil Code section 1942.5 separately limits rent increases after qualifying tenantability events, subject to its conditions and exceptions.
rows.notes: Check the effective date and the statutory conditions; no ranking of defects is established.

rows.label: This building is very likely covered
rows.value: Two rented units in a pre-1979 building is the paradigm Rent Ordinance case; the in-law-unit rule and the 1979 cutoff both point toward coverage rather than exemption
rows.notes: Owner-supplied facts only; confirm in the Property Information Map.

rows.label: Conservative approach
rows.value: Ordinary annual increase at or under 1.6%, license on file first, 30-day written notice, no additional-occupant charge, and an identical written standard applied to both units
rows.notes: Still not a guarantee against a petition.

rows.label: Why the state/local split changes the to-do list, not the arithmetic
rows.value: Because the duty is local, the pre-notice gate is a Rent Board Portal submission and the licence it generates - there is no state agency to apply to, no state filing fee, and no state approval to wait for. The 1.6% arithmetic and the notice rules are unaffected by which level of government imposed the licence duty
rows.notes: The 2023 state law (SB 567) matters to just cause and to units covered only by the state cap; it is not the source of the Rent Board duty (LIC-11, LIC-12, Q-22, Q-23).

rows.label: The one missing fact that most changes the decision
rows.value: Unit 2's increase history since June 1, 2019. Whether annual increases were imposed and on which dates decides (a) whether anything is banked at all, (b) whether the 24-full-months banking rule is met, (c) the anniversary date that fixes the earliest lawful effective date, and (d) how the pending File 261020 proposal, if enacted, would bite. Every other open item is smaller
rows.notes: No figure is computed from the missing history; the Banked increases rows stay blank and flagged (T03-F06, F30). Suggested fix on the Site Suggestions page: SG-11 and SG-05.
